title: Implement Browser Tab Switching Detection and Focus Monitoring

requirements.text: Create a useFocusMonitor React hook that tracks page visibility changes using the Page Visibility API (visibilitychange event) and window focus/blur events (window.onblur and window.onfocus), recording timestamps whenever the user leaves and returns to the page

quotes: Detects when the browser tab becomes inactive or hidden using the Page Visibility API (visibilitychange)
Detects when the user leaves or returns to the browser window using window.onblur and window.onfocus
Records timestamps whenever the user leaves and comes back to the page

acceptanceCriteria: Hook listens to document visibilitychange events
Hook listens to window blur and focus events
Timestamps are recorded for each leave and return event
Hook can be imported and used in any React component

requirements.text: In the useFocusMonitor hook, calculate how long the user stayed away from the page by comparing leave and return timestamps, and count how many times the user switches away within a time period (e.g., per minute)

quotes: Calculates how long the user stayed away from the page
Counts how many times the user switches away within a time period (for example per minute)

acceptanceCriteria: Duration away is calculated in seconds or milliseconds
Switch count is tracked and reset per time window (e.g., 2 minutes)
Switching frequency (switches per minute) is calculated and exposed

requirements.text: In the useFocusMonitor hook, implement a distraction score calculation that updates when the user switches tabs frequently (e.g., more than 5 times in 2 minutes), incrementing the score based on switching frequency

quotes: If the user switches tabs frequently (e.g., more than 5 times in 2 minutes), update a "Distraction Score" variable on the frontend

acceptanceCriteria: Distraction score is a numeric value that increases with frequent switching
Threshold of 5 switches in 2 minutes triggers score increase
Score is exposed by the hook for consumption by components

requirements.text: Display a small on-screen warning component when the distraction score threshold is exceeded, showing a message like 'Frequent tab switching detected. Try focusing for a few minutes.' with dismissible functionality

quotes: Display a small on-screen warning like: "Frequent tab switching detected. Try focusing for a few minutes."

acceptanceCriteria: Warning component appears when distraction threshold is exceeded
Message is clear and non-intrusive (toast or subtle notification)
Warning can be dismissed by the user
Warning does not block the user interface

requirements.text: Send the distraction score and switching statistics (tab switch count, time away, timestamps) to the backend using a POST request to an API endpoint, transmitting data in JSON format whenever significant changes occur

quotes: Send the distraction score and switching statistics to a backend API endpoint using fetch() in JSON format

acceptanceCriteria: POST request sends JSON payload with distraction score, switch count, time away, and timestamp
Request is sent after user returns or at regular intervals
Backend actor receives and stores the data
No personal content, keystrokes, or page content is transmitted

requirements.text: Create a backend Motoko function to record focus monitoring data including distraction score, tab switch count, time away from page, and timestamp, storing this data in the existing backend storage structure

quotes: The backend should receive data sent from the frontend: tab switch count, distraction score, time away from page, timestamp

acceptanceCriteria: Backend function accepts distraction score, switch count, time away, and timestamp parameters
Data is stored in a way that links to user sessions or activity logs
Function returns success or error response
Privacy requirement: no page content or keystrokes are stored

requirements.text: Add inline code comments to the useFocusMonitor hook explaining each section including event listener setup, timestamp recording, duration calculation, switch counting, distraction score logic, and API communication, ensuring the code is beginner-friendly and modifiable

quotes: Also include comments explaining each part of the code so I can easily understand and modify it. The code should be clean, beginner-friendly, and ready to paste into an existing webpage

acceptanceCriteria: Each major section of the hook has a descriptive comment
Comments explain why certain logic is implemented (e.g., why thresholds are chosen)
Variable names are clear and self-documenting
Hook is easy to integrate into any component

constraints: Do not record page content, keystrokes, user inputs, or personal data
Only track focus state, timestamps, and switch counts
Do not modify existing hooks in frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.ts, useInternetIdentity.tsx, useActor.ts, or main.tsx
Do not edit components in frontend/src/components/ui
Use existing backend actor structure for data storage
nonGoals: Recording browser history or visited URLs
Tracking mouse movements or keyboard inputs
Creating new authentication system (Internet Identity already exists)
Implementing SQLite database (use existing Motoko storage)
Adding charts or graphs for tab switching data (dashboard already exists)
